title: Freya and the Sigil
premise: Oscar Hartwell, runaway apprentice of the hedge-witch Freya Vane, has built a careful new life keeping ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Things — a smugglers' guild trafficking in relics, curses, and small miracles. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin to be answered again, the guild's wares turn lethal, the free cities erupt in fervor, and the usurper King Aldous marches to seize the divine power for himself. Oscar discovers the answered prayers are bleeding through a broken covenant Freya once helped shatter, and that the sigil branded on his own hand — the mark of his apprenticeship — is the last surviving key to reforging it. Pursued by the usurper's inquisitors and betrayed by the guildmaster who sold him out, Oscar must reunite with Freya, gather the covenant's scattered oath-bearers, and sacrifice the ledger-bound life he built: in the end, he reforges the covenant at the cost of his own name, erasing himself from every record and memory but Freya's, who alone chooses to remember him.
about_author: Elodie Kavanagh is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing merchant ledgers in port cities before turning to fiction. She writes fantasies about paperwork, power, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar balances the guild's books in the free city of Corvane, cataloguing relics that shouldn't exist. He is meticulous, anonymous, and quietly proud of his invisibility. When a crate of 'answered prayers' arrives still warm and weeping, his careful order cracks. Emotional beat: the comfort of a hidden life, and the first tremor of dread.

chapters.title: What the Gods Left in the Crates
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Investigating the crate, Oscar finds a prayer-slip addressed by name — to him — answered in a hand he recognizes as Freya's. The guildmaster, Serel, orders the crate destroyed and Oscar watched. That night, the sigil on Oscar's hand burns and shows him a burning bridge between realms. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into compulsion; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Proclamation
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Maren Voss's POV. King Aldous declares the returning gods a plague and himself their appointed censor; his armies march on the free cities. Voss, who genuinely believes order is mercy, is sent to Corvane to find 'the sigil-bearer.' Emotional beat: chilling conviction — the antagonist who thinks she is kind.

chapters.title: Runaway, Again
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Serel sells Oscar's location to Voss's agents; the guildhouse burns. Oscar flees with the ledger and the prayer-slip, realizing his apprenticeship sigil is why the gods can find him. Emotional beat: the collapse of the identity he built, and the bitter recognition that running is the one skill he never lost.

chapters.title: The Hedge at the End of the Road
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with a flashback to his apprenticeship. Oscar finds Freya Vane living in deliberate obscurity, unaged in ways that unsettle him. She confirms the covenant she helped break and refuses to help — until the sigil's burn marks begin spelling out the usurper's name. Emotional beat: reunion thick with resentment, guilt, and unfinished love in its broadest sense.

chapters.title: A History Written in Oaths
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya recounts the covenant: seven oath-bearers, mortal and divine, who once kept the realms' borders permeable but just; her faction broke it to cage a god who demanded too much sacrifice. The returning prayers are the cage failing. Emotional beat: confession as burden — power's corruption shown through good intentions.

chapters.title: The First Oath-Bearer
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In the drowned quarter of Corvane, they find Tammas Oduya, a ferryman who has carried the same passenger for forty years — a river god diminished to a whisper. Tammas agrees to help if they recover his oath-token from the guild's seized warehouses. Emotional beat: weary hope; divinity surviving in small stubborn acts.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Mercy
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss interrogates captured guild smugglers and finds Serel, who offers Oscar's ledger in exchange for his life. Reading it, Voss realizes the 'impossible things' were mostly people's desperate prayers — and that Aldous plans not to censor the gods but to enslave them. Emotional beat: the first hairline fracture in her certainty.

chapters.title: The Market of Answered Prayers
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The free cities have erupted in god-fever; a black market sells miracles at ruinous prices, and a mob nearly kills Oscar as a 'sigil thief.' Freya saves him with a working that costs her years of life. Emotional beat: power and its corruption mirrored in ordinary people; Freya's slow self-spending.

chapters.title: What Serel Knew
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Ambushing Serel's caravan, Oscar reclaims the ledger and learns the guild was founded by a former oath-bearer — and that Serel has been selling oath-tokens to Aldous for a decade. Serel escapes, but the ledger reveals the location of the covenant's anchor-stone. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed; the ledger becomes a weapon instead of a refuge.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At the anchor-stone beneath a flooded chapel, Freya attempts a partial reforging and is nearly unmade; only Oscar's sigil pulls her back. They learn the covenant requires all seven oath-bearers — and that the seventh is the caged god itself, which must consent. Emotional beat: awe and terror at the scale of what they've undertaken.

chapters.title: Voss Defects — Almost
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss confronts Aldous with the truth of his plan; he has her oath-bearer ancestor's token, stolen, and offers her a place at his side. She refuses and flees with the token, hunted by her own former soldiers. Emotional beat: justice outside the law — choosing conscience over the institution that made her.

chapters.title: Three Tokens and a Funeral
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The company gathers tokens from two more oath-bearers, one of whom dies passing hers on, naming Oscar — a runaway apprentice — as her successor. Oscar panics at being made an oath-bearer himself. Emotional beat: unwanted inheritance; identity forced into the open.

chapters.title: The God Who Demanded Too Much
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya descends alone to negotiate with the caged god, Veyra, who has spent a century curdling into something vengeful. Veyra offers to help — in exchange for Freya's remaining years and Oscar's sigil. Freya refuses and barely escapes. Emotional beat: power's corruption embodied; mercy that must be paid for.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Burn
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Aldous's armies sack the outer free cities, harvesting prayers at swordpoint to fuel his god-binding engine. Voss reaches the company and delivers the stolen token and Aldous's battle plans — earning trust only after Tammas's river god vouches for her. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance; the enemy of the enemy is not yet a friend.

chapters.title: The Sigil's Name
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Studying the ledger and the sigil, Oscar discovers the truth: the sigil isn't a mark of apprenticeship but a covenant oath written in his own blood by Freya the night his parents died saving hers — he was always the seventh bearer's vessel. Emotional beat: identity shattered and remade; rage at Freya's silence, then understanding.

chapters.title: March of the Censor
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Aldous's vanguard reaches the last free city; Serel, fully corrupted, leads the inquisitors to the anchor-stone. The company splits: some defend the city, some race to the stone. Emotional beat: dread and resolve; every thread tightening toward a single night.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Anchor-Stone
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At the flooded chapel, Serel begins a false reforging with Aldous's harvested prayers, and the caged god breaks free into his body. Freya, Tammas, Voss, and the oath-bearers fight through; Tammas dies holding the ferry-gate open. Emotional beat: desperate, costly heroism — the midpoint sacrifice that makes the ending possible.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. With the true tokens assembled, Oscar offers his sigil and his name to the covenant; Veyra, confronted with the memory of what she was, consents. The covenant reforges through him — but the price is erasure from all record and memory. Emotional beat: transcendence and grief fused; the climax paid in identity itself.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Man
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Aldous, cut off from his stolen divinity, falls to his own armies; Voss chooses exile over power, carrying the truth into the world. The realms settle into a new covenant of consent. But no one remembers Oscar — except Freya, whom the covenant cannot touch, because she wrote his name. Emotional beat: hollow victory; love as the one ledger that cannot be burned.

chapters.title: What Freya Kept
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya rebuilds her hedge at the end of the road and begins writing a book: Oscar's story, in full, against the covenant's silence. Voss visits, bringing the recovered guild ledger as a gift. Emotional beat: mourning braided with purpose — memory as an act of justice.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV — the only chapter in his voice since the reforging. Somewhere between the realms, a nameless ferryman carries a passenger who asks his name. He finds he has one after all: Freya wrote it down, and what is truly written cannot be unwritten. He turns the boat toward the hedge at the end of the road. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope — the ending that rewards the whole journey.
